title: Site/scanner disparity + bias analysis across splits
context: The site-confounding audit in pathology-image-benchmarks-splits-001 tests whether site is recoverable across the train/test split boundary. A deeper fairness and bias analysis extends this: measuring performance disparities across submitting sites, scanner vendors, and (where aggregate metadata is available) demographic proxies recorded in open-access imaging metadata. This is a research-level analysis to surface systematic biases and scanner/site disparities in model performance — not patient-facing, but important for honest benchmarking. Extends the site-confounding audit. Domain-reviewer sign-off required.
objective: Conduct a site/scanner disparity and bias analysis across the benchmark splits: stratify baseline model performance by submitting site, scanner vendor, and any other available aggregate split variables; measure and report performance disparities with statistical context; identify whether certain sites or scanners are systematically harder for the baselines; surface findings honestly in a report rather than hiding them. Extends the site-confounding audit from pathology-image-benchmarks-splits-001.
acceptanceCriteria: Baseline model performance is stratified by submitting site and scanner vendor; per-stratum metrics are reported with sample counts and confidence intervals or variance.
Performance disparities across sites/scanners are measured and reported; any statistically meaningful disparity is surfaced and discussed, not hidden.
Findings are framed as research benchmarking, not clinical conclusions; 'not for clinical or diagnostic use' is stated.
The analysis builds on and extends the site-confounding audit from pathology-image-benchmarks-splits-001, providing deeper stratification.
Domain-reviewer sign-off on the analysis methodology and conclusions is recorded in the governance log.
A report is committed via PR (e.g. docs/analysis/fairness-report.md).
output: A site/scanner disparity and bias analysis report (committed via PR) with per-stratum performance metrics, disparity findings, and domain-reviewer sign-off.
